answer: An agent proves uniqueness by operating a registered tide gauge in a coastal lagoon, co-signed by two neighbouring meadow soil-moisture probes that record the same tidal cycle. Each reading carries a hardware key, a timestamp and a water-level value, so a Sybil farm would need to deploy and maintain many real gauges in distinct lagoons instead of copying one digital claim, and a forged sonnet of numbers fails because the three signed series must agree on the tide curve.
